headline.caveat: ~$1B/year for a custom 1.2-trillion-parameter Gemini model powering the rebuilt Siri; multi-year, exact term undisclosed

realized_to_date.caveat: payments began with the Jan 2026 agreement; nothing disclosed

nature_md: Reported by Bloomberg in Nov 2025 and finalized/confirmed Jan 2026: Apple pays Google ~$1B per year to license a custom 1.2T-parameter Gemini model as the foundation of the rebuilt Siri and next-generation Apple Intelligence, served through Apple's Private Cloud Compute (Apple-silicon servers anonymize traffic; no training on user data). Ends Apple's build-vs-buy ambiguity for frontier AI, and inverts the direction of the famous search ISA (where Google pays Apple ~$20B/yr): Apple now pays Google for AI while Google pays Apple for search defaults — the two flows are legally separate but strategically entangled. The clearest large price point for app-layer model licensing.

accounting.payer_treatment_md: Operating expense (licensing/cloud services) — immaterial to Apple's P&L (~0.1% of opex) but strategically decisive; Apple avoided the multi-GW capex path entirely, making it the only mega-cap consumer platform renting frontier AI rather than building it.
accounting.payee_treatment_md: For Alphabet: licensing/services revenue (~$1B/yr) — small in dollars, large as validation that Gemini wins head-to-head evaluations (Apple tested OpenAI and Anthropic alternatives). Distribution on ~2B devices also has non-cash strategic value no line item captures.
